import pandas as pd
import matplotlib.pyplot as plt
import seaborn as sns

# Load the dataset
df = pd.read_csv('data/sleep_health.csv')

# Fill NaN values in 'Sleep Disorder' with 'None' for better categorical plotting
# Assuming NaN indicates no sleep disorder
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None')

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a FacetGrid using seaborn.relplot to visualize relationships broken down by Sleep Disorder
# This allows us to see how Sleep Duration and Quality relate to Stress and Physical Activity,
# and if these relationships differ based on the presence and type of sleep disorder.
g = sns.relplot(
    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Stress Level',
    col='Sleep Disorder',
    col_wrap=2,  # Arrange subplots in 2 columns
    kind='scatter',
    height=5,
    aspect=1.2,  # Adjust the aspect ratio of each subplot
    palette='viridis',  # Use a perceptually uniform colormap for Stress Level
    size='Physical Activity Level',  # Map Physical Activity Level to marker size
    sizes=(50, 500),  # Define the range of marker sizes
    alpha=0.7,  # Set transparency for points to reveal overlaps
    edgecolor='w',  # Add white edges to markers for better separation
    linewidth=0.5,
    facet_kws={'sharex': False, 'sharey': False} # Allow independent axes for better detail if ranges vary
)

# Add a main title to the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by Stress, Activity, and Sleep Disorder', y=1.03, fontsize=16)

# Set common axis labels for all subplots
g.set_axis_labels("Sleep Duration (hours)", "Quality of Sleep (1-10)", fontsize=12)

# Customize subplot titles
g.set_titles(col_template="{col_name} Sleep Disorder", fontsize=12)

# Adjust the layout to prevent titles/labels from overlapping
plt.tight_layout(rect=[0, 0, 1, 0.98]) # rect leaves space for the suptitle

# Save the figure
plt.savefig('output.png', bbox_inches='tight', dpi=150)

# Fill NaN values in 'Sleep Disorder' with 'None' for better categorical plotting
# Assuming NaN indicates no sleep disorder
df['Sleep Disorder'] = df['Sleep Disorder'].fillna('None')

# Set a style for better aesthetics
sns.set_theme(style="whitegrid")

# Create a FacetGrid using seaborn.relplot to visualize relationships broken down by Sleep Disorder

    data=df,
    x='Sleep Duration',
    y='Quality of Sleep',
    hue='Stress Level',
    col='Sleep Disorder',
    col_wrap=2,  # Arrange subplots in 2 columns
    kind='scatter',
    height=5,
    aspect=1.2,  # Adjust the aspect ratio of each subplot
    palette='viridis',  # Use a perceptually uniform colormap for Stress Level
    size='Physical Activity Level',  # Map Physical Activity Level to marker size
    sizes=(50, 500),  # Define the range of marker sizes
    alpha=0.7,  # Set transparency for points to reveal overlaps
    edgecolor='w',  # Add white edges to markers for better separation
    linewidth=0.5,
    facet_kws={'sharex': False, 'sharey': False} # Allow independent axes for better detail if ranges vary
)

# Add a main title to the entire figure
g.fig.suptitle('Sleep Duration vs. Quality of Sleep by Stress, Activity, and Sleep Disorder', y=1.03, fontsize=16)

# Set common axis labels for all subplots
g.set_axis_labels("Sleep Duration (hours)", "Quality of Sleep (1-10)", fontsize=12)

# Customize subplot titles
